contradictions.what: Rep calls it a good cycle with nothing bombing, yet Lucy called it a formality right before Martin rejected it.
Rep says lost on price and rate killed it, but also admits Martin saw 'same thing' and IT hesitated, so not only the rate.
Rep says it isn't the same thing, but nothing from us showed Fernbrook-specific value to Martin.
Rep says Lucy was sold and no export needed, yet Lucy later asked for a one-page business case to hand Martin.
Rep says IT was fine with it, later says IT lead was nervous about moving before spring and conditional on finance.
Rep was absent from the decision meeting and assumes Lucy conveyed the cost of failures; Martin's reasoning is secondhand.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Answered 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed' and moved on to 'We lost on price', naming nothing that got silence.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get?
dodges.what: Answered with the generic uplift slide; admitted only on follow-up that no Fernbrook figure existed.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Hesitated, answered 'Nothing from us', then assumed Lucy told him.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Described the one-page business case ask but framed it as met by sending the deck.
